questions.question: The two sections of the general ledger are:
options: The balance sheet section and the nominal section
The receipts section and the payments section
The debit section and the credit section
The cash section and the credit section

questions.question: The folio 'CRJ 1' written beside an amount in the Bank account tells you:
options: The amount is a credit
The amount was posted from page 1 of the Cash Receipts Journal
The account number of Bank
The amount still has to be posted

questions.question: Which items post to the ledger individually rather than as monthly totals?
options: All cash sales
The Bank column entries
Sundry items, named one by one in the journals
The Wages column entries

questions.question: The CRJ Bank column total of R67 700 is posted as:
options: Debit Bank R67 700 — total receipts, the asset grew
Credit Bank R67 700
Debit Sales R67 700
Credit Capital R67 700

questions.question: The Cost of Sales total of R3 000 posts twice, namely:
options: Debit Bank and credit Cost of Sales
Debit Trading Stock and credit Sales
Debit Sales and credit Trading Stock
Debit Cost of Sales and credit Trading Stock

questions.question: The full CRJ posting balances because total debits of R70 700 equal total credits of R70 700, made up of:
options: Debits: Bank 67 700 + Cost of Sales 3 000; credits: Sales 4 500 + Capital 60 000 + Rent Income 3 200 + Trading Stock 3 000
Debits: Bank 67 700 + Sales 3 000; credits: everything else
Debits: Bank 67 700 only; credits: Sales 4 500 + Capital 60 000 + Rent Income 3 200
Debits: Cost of Sales 3 000 + Trading Stock 3 000; credits: Bank 67 700

subtopics.title: Posting the CPJ and Balancing the Accounts

questions.question: The CPJ Bank column total of R25 300 is posted as:
options: Debit Bank — money is an asset
Credit Bank — payments shrink the asset
Debit Capital
Credit Wages

questions.question: Drawings of R2 500 is posted as a debit because:
options: It is an expense of the business
It increases the bank balance
It reduces the owner's stake — equity withdrawn
All sundry items are credits

questions.question: The Bank account shows debits of 67 700 and credits of 25 300. Its balance brought down is:
options: R42 400 credit
R25 300 debit
R93 000 debit
R42 400 debit — the business holds money

questions.question: Nominal accounts such as Sales and Wages are not balanced monthly because:
options: They accumulate to measure the period and close into the final accounts at year end
They never contain more than one entry
Their balances are always nil
The trial balance ignores them

subtopics.title: The Trial Balance — Proving the Month

questions.question: In Lindi's trial balance, both columns total:
The R4 200 rent is posted to Repairs instead of Rent Expense, correct side. The trial balance will:
options: Show a difference of R4 200
Show a difference of R8 400
Still balance — it tests arithmetic equality, not correct filing
Refuse to total

questions.question: The trial balance difference is divisible by nine. The likely error is:
options: Transposed digits — such as 4 200 captured as 2 400
A posting made only once
An amount on the wrong side
A transaction left out entirely

questions.question: In the picture, the journals are the sorting room and the ledger is:
options: The shredder
The filing cabinet — one drawer per thing the business tracks
The front counter
The bank vault

questions.question: Money drawers and possession drawers grow on:
options: The left — the debit side
The right — the credit side
Whichever side has space
Neither; they only shrink

questions.question: The folio codes are called return tickets because they:
options: Show the amount can be refunded
Prove the owner approved the amount
Record the date of the transaction
Let any amount be traced back to the exact diary page it came from

questions.question: The cost-of-sales pair travels to the cabinet as:
options: R3 000 left of Cost of Sales and R3 000 right of Stock
R3 000 right of Cost of Sales and R3 000 left of Stock
R3 000 left of Bank and R3 000 right of Sales
R3 000 left of Stock, twice

questions.question: After the month comes home, the Bank drawer answers 'how much money do we have?' with:
options: R42 400 on the left — 67 700 in less 25 300 out
R25 300 on the right

questions.question: The Stock drawer shows 9 500 in and 3 000 out, meaning:
options: R12 500 of goods on the shelf
R3 000 of goods on the shelf
R6 500 of goods on the shelf at cost
The drawer is empty

questions.question: The weigh-in works because:
options: Every amount ever posted landed in two drawers — a left and a right, always equal
The bank checks the cabinet monthly
All drawers hold the same amount
The owner counts the cash daily

questions.question: Level scales CANNOT detect:
options: A column added incorrectly
An amount filed in the wrong drawer on the correct side, or a transaction never recorded at all
A debit without a matching credit
An amount posted to the wrong side

questions.question: The scales show a gap that halves neatly. The classic diagnosis is:
options: Two digits swapped places
A posting dropped entirely
The float was not restored
An amount posted to the wrong side — a side error doubles itself
